title: Introduce RBACv2 attribute blacklist, KMS consent mapper, and audit fanout
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Adds RBACv2 attribute-level denylist support, a consent-mapper for multi-KMS routing, and a sampled audit fanout path. No public API surface changes. Admins can opt-in via feature flag.
description: Motivation: Customers asked for a simple, policy-driven way to block known-sensitive attributes from being used in operator- or tenant-scoped RBAC decisions, and for clearer proof of KMS consent when routing encryption requests across providers. This change introduces three cooperating pieces: 1) an attribute-level denylist in the RBACv2 policy evaluator (configurable per-namespace or global), 2) a KMS consent mapper that binds service/operator claims to an explicit consent token and preferred KMS region/provider, and 3) an audit fanout pipeline that can sample, redact, and forward audit events to multiple sinks (internal ledger + compliance S3 + SIEM) with deduplication. Design summary: - Attribute denylist: a lightweight predicate that runs during policy normalization and rejects or tags attributes that match denylist patterns. The denylist supports exact values, prefix/suffix, and regex with explicit allow-overrides. - KMS consent mapper: small middleware in the crypto allocator. If a request has an operator/service claim that maps to a consent profile, we attach a signed consent-reference header and prefer the listed KMS providers in order. Consent lookup is cached with TTL=5m and has an opt-out fallback to default KMS. - Audit fanout: new audit adapter that accepts canonical audit envelopes, applies provenance stamping, optional PII redaction rules tied to the denylist, and forwards to multiple configured sinks with sampling rules per-sink. Deduplication uses a short-lived HMAC-based fingerprint. Backwards compatibility: feature gated under admin flag "rbacv2-attr-denylist" and runtime flag "audit-fanout-v1". No changes to public REST API. Linear/Jira refs: ENG-9311 (policy), SEC-140 (kms-consent), COMPL-22 (audit). Checklist: - [x] Policy format addition and parser tests - [x] Middleware integration tests - [x] End-to-end KMS consent flow test with mock providers - [x] Audit fanout unit tests + integration with sample SIEM sink - [x] Documentation added to security playbook - [x] Feature flags wired and documented Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to staging with flags off and run policy/consent smoke tests. 2) Enable denylist in shadow mode (tagging only) for 48h to collect metrics. 3) Enable enforcement for a small set of tenants (canary). 4) Gradually expand and enable audit-fanout in passive mode, then active forwarding. Monitoring: Added metrics rbac.attr_denylist.matches, kms.consent.miss/hit, audit.fanout.forwarded_by_sink, audit.fanout.fingerprints_deduped. Impact/risk: Low-medium. Denylist misconfiguration could block legitimate actions — mitigated by allow-overrides and shadow mode. KMS consent mapping errors fall back to default KMS. CI: all unit/integration tests pass in this branch. Notes: This PR intentionally keeps policy syntax conservative; a follow-up will add a small UI for denylist management in the Console.

3 commits:
- Add attribute denylist data model, parser, and unit tests
- Implement KMS consent mapper middleware and caching layer
- Add audit fanout adapter, sampling and dedupe logic; update config docs

risk_assessment: Medium: new enforcement could block flows if denylist misconfigured. Mitigations: shadow mode, allow-overrides, incremental rollout, and quick rollback via feature flags.
